content: Chloramphenicol can significantly alter the metabolism of various drugs by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal enzymes, particularly CYP3A4. This interaction can lead to increased drug levels and effects, necessitating careful monitoring, dose adjustments, or the use of alternative therapies. Below are specific examples of these interactions: 1. Oliceridine: Chloramphenicol increases oliceridine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration is necessary, reduce oliceridine dosing frequency and monitor for respiratory depression and sedation. Adjust subsequent doses as needed. If chloramphenicol is discontinued, consider increasing the oliceridine dose to achieve stable effects while monitoring for opioid withdrawal. 2. Omaveloxolone: Chloramphenicol raises omaveloxolone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 50 mg/day if unavoidable. Monitor closely and discontinue if adverse effects occur. 3. Ombitasvir/Paritaprevir/Ritonavir: Chloramphenicol increases the levels of this combination therapy by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative drug. 4. Osilodrostat: Chloramphenicol elevates osilodrostat levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Reduce the osilodrostat dose by half when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors and monitor closely. 5. Oxycodone: Chloramphenicol increases oxycodone levels through CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor for enhanced effects. 6. Paclitaxel Protein-Bound: Chloramphenicol raises paclitaxel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Pacritinib: Chloramphenicol significantly increases pacritinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated. 8. Palbociclib: Chloramphenicol elevates palbociclib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 9. Paricalcitol: Chloramphenicol increases paricalcitol levels through CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Pazopanib: Chloramphenicol significantly increases pazopanib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated. 11. Pexidartinib: Chloramphenicol raises pexidartinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or reduce the pexidartinib dose if unavoidable. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor. 12. Phenobarbital: Chloramphenicol increases phenobarbital levels by reducing its metabolism, while phenobarbital decreases chloramphenicol levels by enhancing its metabolism. Monitor closely as the significance is uncertain. 13. Phenytoin: Chloramphenicol increases phenytoin levels by inhibiting its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Pimavanserin: Chloramphenicol elevates pimavanserin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 15. Pimozide: Chloramphenicol increases pimozide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 16. Pirtobrutinib: Chloramphenicol raises pirtobrutinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or reduce the pirtobrutinib dose by 50 mg if unavoidable. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor. 17. Polatuzumab Vedotin: Chloramphenicol increases polatuzumab vedotin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely, as its active metabolite (MMAE) is a CYP3A4 substrate. 18. Ponatinib: Chloramphenicol elevates ponatinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or reduce the ponatinib dose to the next lower level. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing chloramphenicol. 19. Pralsetinib: Chloramphenicol increases pralsetinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 20. Progesterone (Natural): Chloramphenicol raises progesterone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Quetiapine: Chloramphenicol increases quetiapine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 22. Quizartinib: Chloramphenicol elevates quizartinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Reduce the dose or interrupt treatment during co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the inhibitor. 23. Ranolazine: Chloramphenicol significantly increases ranolazine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated. 24. Red Yeast Rice: Chloramphenicol raises red yeast rice levels by inhibiting CYP3A4, increasing the risk of myopathy or rhabdomyolysis. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 25. Regorafenib: Chloramphenicol significantly increases regorafenib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated. 26. Repaglinide: Chloramphenicol elevates repaglinide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Ribociclib: Chloramphenicol increases ribociclib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or reduce the ribociclib dose to 400 mg/day if unavoidable. 28. Rimegepant: Chloramphenicol raises rimegepant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 29. Ripretinib: Chloramphenicol increases ripretinib levels and its active metabolite (DP-5439) by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Ritonavir: Chloramphenicol elevates ritonavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 31. Rivaroxaban: Chloramphenicol increases rivaroxaban levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Roflumilast (Topical): Chloramphenicol raises roflumilast levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Romidepsin: Chloramphenicol increases romidepsin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Ruxolitinib: Chloramphenicol elevates ruxolitinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or reduce the ruxolitinib dose in patients with myelofibrosis or polycythemia vera. No dose adjustment is needed for graft-versus-host disease. 35. Saxagliptin: Chloramphenicol increases saxagliptin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 36. Seladelpar: Chloramphenicol raises seladelpar levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely, especially in poor CYP2C9 metabolizers. 37. Selpercatinib: Chloramphenicol increases selpercatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 38. Selumetinib: Chloramphenicol elevates selumetinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or reduce the selumetinib dose if unavoidable. 39. Sildenafil: Chloramphenicol increases sildenafil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 40. Siponimod: Chloramphenicol raises siponimod levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors combined with CYP2C9 inhibitors. 41. Sirolimus: Chloramphenicol increases sirolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 42. Sodium Picosulfate/Magnesium Oxide/Anhydrous Citric Acid: Chloramphenicol reduces the efficacy of this combination by altering colonic bacterial flora. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Sofosbuvir/Velpatasvir: Chloramphenicol increases sofosbuvir/velpatasvir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Sonidegib: Chloramphenicol elevates sonidegib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 45. Sparsentan: Chloramphenicol increases sparsentan levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or interrupt sparsentan treatment if unavoidable. 46. Sufentanil: Chloramphenicol raises sufentanil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 47. Sunitinib: Chloramphenicol increases sunitinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 48. Suvoxerant: Chloramphenicol significantly increases suvoxerant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated. 49. Tacrolimus: Chloramphenicol elevates tacrolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 50. Tamsulosin: Chloramphenicol increases tamsulosin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated. 51. Tasimetleon: Chloramphenicol raises tasimetleon levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Tazemetostat: Chloramphenicol increases tazemetostat levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 53. Temsirolimus: Chloramphenicol elevates temsirolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 54. Terbinafine: Chloramphenicol increases terbinafine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Tezacaftor: Chloramphenicol raises tezacaftor levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 56. Tinidazole: Chloramphenicol increases tinidazole levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Tisotumab Vedotin: Chloramphenicol elevates tisotumab vedotin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Tofacitinib: Chloramphenicol increases tofacitinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 59. Tolterodine: Chloramphenicol raises tolterodine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 60. Tolvaptan: Chloramphenicol significantly increases tolvaptan levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated. 61. Toremifene: Chloramphenicol elevates toremifene levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 62. Trabectedin: Chloramphenicol increases trabectedin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 63. Trazodone: Chloramphenicol raises trazodone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 64. Triazolam: Chloramphenicol significantly increases triazolam levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated. 65. Typhoid Vaccine (Live): Chloramphenicol reduces the efficacy of the live typhoid vaccine by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Wait until antibiotic therapy is complete before administering the vaccine. 66. Ubrogepant: Chloramphenicol significantly increases ubrogepant levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated. 67. Ulipristal: Chloramphenicol raises ulipristal levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 68. Umeclidinium Bromide/Vilanterol (Inhaled): Chloramphenicol increases the levels of this combination therapy via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 69. Upadacitinib: Chloramphenicol elevates upadacitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 70. Valbenazine: Chloramphenicol raises valbenazine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce the valbenazine dose and monitor closely. 71. Vamorolone: Chloramphenicol increases vamorolone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Reduce the starting dose and monitor closely. 72. Vardenafil: Chloramphenicol elevates vardenafil levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce the dose if co-administered with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 73. Velpatasvir: Chloramphenicol raises velpatasvir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 74. Vemurafenib: Chloramphenicol increases vemurafenib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 75. Venetoclax: Chloramphenicol significantly elevates venetoclax levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration during the ramp-up phase in CLL/SLL patients. Adjust the dose and monitor closely in AML patients. 76. Venlafaxine: Chloramphenicol raises venlafaxine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 77. Verapamil: Chloramphenicol increases verapamil levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 78. Vilazodone: Chloramphenicol elevates vilazodone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or reduce the daily dose to 20 mg. 79. Vinblastine: Chloramphenicol raises vinblastine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 80. Vincristine: Chloramphenicol increases vincristine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 81. Vincristine Liposomal: Chloramphenicol elevates vincristine liposomal levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 82. Vinorelbine: Chloramphenicol raises vinorelbine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 83. Voclosporin: Chloramphenicol significantly increases voclosporin levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Co-administration is contraindicated. 84. Vorapaxar: Chloramphenicol elevates vorapaxar levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid co-administration or use an alternative therapy. 85. Warfarin: Chloramphenicol increases warfarin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 and other enzymes. Monitor INR more frequently and adjust the warfarin dose as needed. 86. Zanubrutinib: Chloramphenicol raises zanubrutinib levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Reduce the dose to 80 mg daily and monitor closely. 87. Zolpidem: Chloramphenicol increases zolpidem levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Consider reducing the zolpidem dose and monitor closely. 88. Zonisamide: Chloramphenicol elevates zonisamide levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 89. Zuranolone: Chloramphenicol raises zuranolone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Reduce the dose and monitor closely.
